name: Polycab India Ltd
title: Polycab India Ltd - 542652 - Announcement Under Regulation 30 (LODR) - Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Polycab posted record Q2 FY27 with revenue up 53% and EBITDA margin 14.4%, but capacity is still expanding (EHV plant now FY28), mgmt is not pricing-responding to UltraTech's entry, and working capital at 11 days is flattered by LC-driven payables.

capex.peers_comment: UltraTech's entry into wires; management said its capex and revenue ambition look elusive.
capex.quote: the kind of capex that UltraTech has put into this industry, the kind of revenue guidance that they have given close to around potential of around 6x to 7x, it looks elusive at the moment

triggers.label: UltraTech entering wires market
triggers.quote: UltraTech's entry, I believe that's the peer that you have been referring to.

triggers.label: EHV plant commissioning slips to FY28
triggers.quote: we are expecting the EHV plant to now commission somewhere in FY 2028, the next year, though, so FY28.

triggers.label: Working cycle 11 days via LC payables
triggers.quote: the average working capital cycle reducing to approximately 11 days in second quarter fiscal '27. This was aided by higher payable days

triggers.label: No price action yet vs new entrant
Revenue +53% YoY, volumes mid-high single digit

guidance.quote: we remain confident of sustaining medium - to long -term EBITDA margins within our guided range of 11% to 13%
Our objective continues to be growing at 1.5x to 2x of the industry growth rate
we continue to expect sustainable margins for the EPC business to remain in the high single -digit range
we expect the working capital cycle to trend towards our long-term operating range of 45 to 50 days

red_flags.label: IBC/CIRP admission against company (Asier Metals)
red_flags.quote: the Honorable NCLAT has staye d and kept in abeyance the order of admission in its entirety

red_flags.label: Working capital flattered by LC payables
red_flags.quote: This was aided by higher payable days arising from the increased use of letters of credit

evasions.topic: Wires vs cables segment growth outlook
evasions.quote: I mean we would not like to give any guidance on that. We never share that kind of a guidance.
Your channel chec k is different to probably ours.
So I think we would not like to guide in terms of the revenue growth per se

summary.headline: Polycab Q2 FY27 revenue rose 53% YoY with PAT of INR 9,900 million (+43%) and EBITDA margin of 14.4%, all record highs.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly and half-yearly revenue and profitability, with consolidated revenue up 53% YoY and all segments contributing to growth. EBITDA rose 39% YoY to a 14.4% margin, up more than 50 bps QoQ, helped by mix, operating leverage and copper price pass-through. Wires and Cables grew 47% and FMEG grew 124%, with FMEG crossing a 10% EBIT margin for the first time. Management said the Asier Metals IBC matter is under NCLAT review, with order reserved and no material impact expected.

financial_highlights.value: Growth 53% YoY (value not stated in call)

financial_highlights.change: Up more than 50 bps QoQ; EBITDA +39% YoY
vs INR 29.4 billion a year ago
Aided by higher payable days from increased letters of credit use

segments.name: Wires and Cables
segments.commentary: Revenue +47% YoY; domestic W&C +50% YoY with mid-to-high single-digit volume growth. Wires grew early double digits in volume and cables mid single digits. EBIT margin 14.2%, up sequentially. Exports grew 17% YoY and 85% QoQ, and were about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Revenue +124% YoY, 11th consecutive quarter of industry-leading growth, and seventh consecutive profitable quarter per CEO. EBIT margin 10.1%, first time above double digits. Solar (inverters only, traded) was the main driver; fans premium mix about 33% and lights about 38%.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 6,171 million (+53% YoY), EBIT INR 444 million (7.2% margin). Order book about INR 9,000-10,000 crore, mainly Bharat Net and RDSS projects. Medium-term margin guidance is high single digit.

guidance_outlook: Wires and Cables medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 11% to 13% reiterated; management said it would be happy to run at the higher end.
FMEG target of growing 1.5x to 2x industry growth with margins; long-term EBITDA margin range of 8% to 10% cited for FY30.
Wires and Cables volume growth anchor: 1.5x market growth; at ~7.8% GDP, the segment could grow about 12-13%.
Working capital cycle expected to normalise toward the 45-50 day long-term range.
EHV plant commissioning now expected in FY28 (commissioning may start April or May 2027).
Management declined to guide on revenue growth given copper price volatility.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex of INR 6.1 billion for capacity expansion, supply chain and future growth platforms.
EHV plant commissioning now expected in FY28, not earlier.
Wires and Cables market about INR 1.1 lakh crore; wires about 30% of it, with 30-35% of wires unorganised.
Data centre capacity about 1.6-1.7 GW currently; reports suggest 8-15 GW ahead.
demand_pricing: Domestic W&C volume growth mid-to-high single digits on a strong base (last year's volume growth was about 18%).
Channel sales grew faster than institutional; West largest region, then South, North and East.
Copper prices up about 6% QoQ and about 40-45% on average in H1; pricing is cost-plus with pass-through to customers (monthly for cables, fortnightly for wires).
UltraTech's entry into wires: management said no pricing action taken so far and no channel pricing correction seen.
Export order book strong in US, Europe, LATAM, Asia and Middle East; now selling to 94 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Are FMEG margins and the Wires and Cables margin rise sustainable, and would Project Spring targets be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited scale, operating leverage, premium mix and bundled solution offerings for FMEG. Targets are FY30-based; long-term FMEG EBITDA margin of 8-10% is still cited, and a 10.1% EBIT margin is described as very high.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any pricing response to new wires entrants like UltraTech?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no action on pricing so far, that the entrant's wires presence is a small share of the business, and that the company gained 1-1.5% share annually (3-4 points last year).

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 be soft on a high base, and what is FY volume growth expected to be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly comparisons are not the right lens; the anchor is 1.5x market growth, and volume should be viewed on a 10-12 month basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a seasonal copper-price related inventory build or delay in offtake?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant pickup in channel inventory; copper rose about 6% QoQ and aluminium fell, and restocking follows price moves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 12.5 billion line in the cash flow statement?
qa_highlights.answer: It is advance payments for inventory procurement, not a one-off, roughly INR 1,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Q2 revenue run rate be sustained into H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide revenue, noting copper price movements drive the base and demand is strong.

risks_watch: Asier Metals IBC matter: NCLAT has stayed NCLT's admission and CIRP order; arguments heard on Oct 15, 2026 and order reserved with no date given. Management expects no material impact.
Competition from UltraTech in wires; a channel check reported entrant wires priced 10-15% lower, which management disputed.
Copper price volatility and inventory swings; working capital benefit from letters of credit may reverse.
Export softness from geopolitics and shipping delays of 10-12 days.
Tough Q3 FY27 volume base (last year's Q3 growth was about 40-45%).
Solar inverter growth is a trading model; FMEG profit mix depends on it.
Macro: repo rate raised 25 bps to 5.5% with a calibrated tightening stance.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and margins, with repeated emphasis on record results. Evasive on guidance specifics (revenue, competition pricing, wires vs cables mix, IBC timeline) and deferred to FY30 targets.
key_quotes: Polycab has delivered its highest ever quarterly and half-yearly revenue and profitability.
We do not expect any adverse or material impact on our financial or business operations arising from the said situation.
We are not seeing any sort of pricing correction right now.
So if all things come together, definitely we'll see margins going to north of what we are seeing today.

adds.what: EHV plant (commissioning slipped to FY28; may start April or May 2027)

growth.why: Management declined to guide revenue growth given copper volatility, but reiterated margin ranges (W&C 11-13%, FMEG 1.5-2x industry growth) and cited a 12-13% W&C volume growth potential; backing is partial via a EPC order book of INR 9,000-10,000 crore, the EHV plant slipping to FY28 and channel/export demand, with no specific new capacity numbers given.
